title: weightpack-mismatch-timetrace
content:
Context:
Quick personal breadcrumbs while I chase a recurring model-load failure hitting our private deploy integration tests and sporadically in a customer's Private cluster. Symptoms are: model fails to unpack during startup -> serving runtime falls back to smaller variant, leads to higher latency and OOMs later. Happens ~1:20 runs.

Observed behavior timeline (local repro on dev-box, trimmed):
- 2026-02-25 09:12 UTC: CI job downloads weightpack from GCS path gs://private-models/megabert-v2/weights-v2.tar.snappy (multipart).
- 2026-02-25 09:12:13 UTC: curl returns 200 but Content-Length header = 104857600 (100MiB).
- 2026-02-25 09:12:13.7 UTC: runtime gunzip/snappy-unpack step starts.
- 2026-02-25 09:12:14.5 UTC: unpack error: "unexpected EOF while reading block header".
- 2026-02-25 09:12:14.5 UTC: engine logs: "unpack failed (shard 3): tar: short read on file weights/transformer/p0.bin (wanted 1048576, got 1048574)"
- 2026-02-25 09:12:15 UTC: retry download with range GET and recompose -> succeeds then unpacks OK.

Commands/tried snippets (copied from shell):
- straight curl:
  curl -v -o /tmp/w.tar.snappy "https://storage.googleapis.com/private-models/megabert-v2/weights-v2.tar.snappy"

- range GET around failing shard region (byte offsets approximated):
  curl -H "Range: bytes=31457280-41943039" -o /tmp/part.bin "https://storage.googleapis.com/private-models/megabert-v2/weights-v2.tar.snappy"

- verify local tar header with python:
  python -c "import tarfile,sys; t=tarfile.open('/tmp/w.tar.snappy','r:');
for m in t.getmembers():
    if m.size % 512 != 0:
        print('pad issue',m.name,m.size); sys.exit(0)
print('tar sane')"

- streamed decompression test (to reproduce EOF):
  gzip -d -c /tmp/w.tar.snappy | tar -tvf - 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'

Error snippets from runtime logs: (scrubbed)
- "unpack failed: short read on file weights/transformer/p0.bin (expected 1048576, got 1048574)"
- "http: unexpected EOF reading trailer"
- "gcs: object size 104857600 but bytes written 104857598"
- "tar: file header checksum mismatch for weights/token_embed.bin"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Partial/multipart upload or edge-case GCS chunking -> last chunk occasionally truncated by 2 bytes. Multipart compose bug or a proxy misreporting length. Explains consistent off-by-2.
2) Compression wrapper mismatch: pack pipeline applies snappy framing but at runtime we call gzip stream. Mismatch would be larger failure, but note the header checksums sometimes indicate tar header corruption only on specific files.
3) Network proxy/timeouts when streaming large object -> client stops before trailer; but Content-Length present so curl usually blocks until done. Intermittent proxies could send TCP FIN early.
4) Tar padding off-by-two due to wrong block alignment in our pack step (we do size rounding to 512 blocks but code path for shard 3 had old rounding algorithm).
5) Object metadata reports size before finalization (object size is precompose), downstream clients reading before compose completes.

What makes me lean to hypothesis 1 and 4:
- Off-by-2 is suspiciously small and reproducible on the same shard index.
- Re-downloading with Range HEAD/GET consistently returns correct bytes.
- Running gsutil cp followed by sha256sum on the object occasionally differs from the HTTP GET copy, suggesting different serving path (gcs internal compose vs signed-url path).

Repro steps to run locally (short checklist):
- Start small local HTTP server to emulate truncated object: python -m http.server 8000 (replace listener to close connection early with small script).
- Re-run runtime unpack against it to reproduce "short read".
- Use gcs rewriting tool to compose with explicit chunk sizes and verify final object size with gsutil stat.
- Run pack step locally with new padding code (branch: dev/pack-fix-align) and create a tar with custom padding values, then unpack with our runtime.

Temporary mitigations we've applied:
- Automatic range re-get on detect EOF: when tar unpack fails due to short read, runtime will re-request offending byte range and retry unpack in-memory for that file. (PR: GH-rlw/1264)
- Add a brief 300ms sleep and reattempt to download signed URL if Content-Length vs reported bytes mismatch.

Notes for next debugging targets / TODOs: (my own TODOs)
- [ ] Add logging to pack pipeline to emit per-file size and block rounding used (exact bytes before compression).
- [ ] Add instrumentation in download client to compute incremental sha256 as bytes stream in and compare to object metadata if present.
- [ ] Reproduce with a deterministic small tar where we intentionally append 2 zero bytes and confirm runtime failure mode.
- [ ] Check if any customers upload model artifacts via AWS S3 -> cross-object compose path might be different. Add telemetry for upload method in object metadata.
- [ ] Audit code handling for snappy vs gzip; ensure content-type indicates framing and runtime uses right decompressor.

Loose thoughts / heuristics:
- If it's a compose bug on the provider side, the 'range GET' pattern will be the fastest mitigation. We should prefer range-retry only for private deploys where network is less reliable.
- Small padding bugs are a classic source of flaky CI failures; adding sanity checks to the pack step would reduce mean time to detect.

Slack breadcrumbs / threads to check: slack:#infra-weightfetch (search 'short read' around Feb 25), convo with @Ivy (ran gsutil compose tests), @Rohan validated that their macOS client also got off-by-2 when pulling via signed URL from a certain region.

If I get time today: instrument the pack job to write a .manifest.json next to the tar with per-file sizes and sha256. That will let the runtime detect mismatch without full retry.

End notes: putting this here so I have a single place to copy into GH issue and the customer incident timeline. Will update after reproducer runs.

-- Devon
